summary.intent: Get started on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, decide on a product direction (a recheck-and-act agent), prepare office-hours/interview material, and build a polling watcher with an LLM analysis agent.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found the Collector's Edition misses Sunday despite the plan saying all ok, published a findings doc and briefing page plus a Felix interview doc, and built and committed a Python watcher package (poller, versioned store, extractor, pluggable LLM agent, notifiers) with a baseline poll run against the real portal.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder (raw, drops, notes, img, store); .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored, while .env.example is committed with an empty token.
Portal API has only three endpoints (GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path}, /archive.zip) with no notification or webhook; the documented approach is to poll the file list and compare SHA-256 checksums.
Existing portal files can be replaced under the same name and formats may change, so change detection must use checksums and extraction cannot assume a fixed layout.
Teammates added CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md with a team workflow; tasks are claimed via a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md before building.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no modified files log 'skipping checkpoint', and Codex hooks need approval via /hooks.

code.finding: Large first syncs use archive.zip instead of per-file downloads, and portal requests have retries added after the baseline poll failed.

Polling loop lists files, compares checksums, stores versions in a checksum-keyed blob store plus SQLite log, and hands changed files to the LLM agent and notifiers; baseline poll can run without a model.

workflow: Use a subagent for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations, 59 scans) while the main session continues reading other data.
Render scanned PDFs to images to read them; scans revealed discrepancies that structured data hid (e.g. 80,000 vs handwritten 8,000 art books).
Keep tests on invented data with fake portal and LLM responses so no confidential data or API calls are involved.
Commit in separate topics with the user's author identity set via env vars and no session trailer.

friction: Portal token was empty at the start, blocking data access until the user supplied it.
Initial baseline poll failed on a large number of files, requiring archive.zip and retry logic.
Computer went to sleep mid-response, leaving the README/.env.example documentation step possibly incomplete.
The first commit attempt needed a retry to apply the correct author via env vars.
Unclear whether portal data and supplier replies differ per team; needs asking the Lio engineers.
The SessionStart hook was logged under a different session ID, which looked like missing hooks.
open_items: Update the briefing page and doc with the 14:37 drop; they still show the 14:00 state.
Register sender email addresses in the portal Settings and set up an inbox the agent can send from and read replies in.
Draft and send the approved Polish order to Karton Nowak for 8,000 art books before the 24h offer expires, then reply to Boise about EXW terms.
Build the reconcile-and-act agent with one-click approval and a recompute step in plain code.
Decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc now that the page exists.
Ask Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
Change the portal password shared in Discord after the hack.
